about.text: Robiola is an Italian soft-ripened cheese of the stracchino family. It is from the Langhe region and made with varying proportions of cow's, goat's, and sheep's milk. One theory is that the cheese gets its name from the comune (municipality) of Robbio, in the province of Pavia; another that the name comes from the word rubeole (ruddy) because of the color of the seasoned rind.

how.label: set with lactic
how.text: A long, cool, mostly lactic set gives a soft, acidic, creamy paste with live lactic bacteria that is never cooked or pressed. If left longer, natural moulds on the surface turn it creamy under the rind and give it a more pronounced taste.

steps.note: Set lactic with animal rennet, and an optional local natural milk or whey starter.

steps.name: mould
steps.note: In cylindrical plastic moulds, turned; 10–14 cm across, 250–400 g.
Fresco is ready after 3–10 d, affinato after more than 10 d, when natural moulds bloom on the surface.
